item.description: On November 24 th , join Homeless Connect Toronto at the Toronto Reference Library for a special premiere screening and community conversation celebrating the launch of Seeking Shelter, a documentary series by filmmaker Nadine Valcin. As Canada continues to grapple with a growing housing crisis, Seeking Shelter shines a light on the people, organizations, and grassroots movements creating innovative and inclusive solutions to housing instability. Through stories of resilience, collaboration, and community action, the series explores what becomes possible when people come together to reimagine housing. item.title: Noirvember Film Screening: Double Indemnity (1944) — Tue Nov 24, 6:00 PM — North York Central Library
item.description:
Noirvember is an annual, month-long celebration of film noir. Join the Languages, Literature, and Fine Arts Department for a screening of one of the defining works of the genre, Billy Wilder's Double Indemnity (1944). All are welcome. Drop-in until capacity is reached. Rating: G Release Year: 1944 Running Time: 107 minutes Synopsis (Audio Ciné Films): Unsuspecting Mr. Dietrichson becomes increasingly accident prone after his icily calculating wife encourages him to sign a double-indemnity policy proposed by a smooth talking insurance agent. Against a backdrop of distinctly Californian settings, the partners-in-crime plan the perfect murder to collect on the insurance. Perfect until a claims manager gets a familiar feeling of foul play and pursues the matter relentlessly. Tension soars as the would-be lovers find themselves plotting against each other.

item.title: Planetary perspectives in knowledge co-production between the global South and North: reflections on the potential and challenges of Experiential Education — Wed Nov 25, 2:30 PM — HNES 141
item.description: This presentation by Dr. Angela Stienen, EUC Scholar-in-Residence, introduces an innovative approach to experiential education and planetary learning, developed within a long-standing research partnership between the University of Antioquia in Medellín, Colombia, and the University of Education in Bern, Switzerland. The approach draws on Latin American critical theory and on the experience of Colombia’s Movimiento Pedagógico Nacional, a large-scale social movement of the 1980s and 1990s which organized so-called National Educational Expeditions: researchers and university professors, activists, school teachers and students explored together the relation between neoliberal educational restructuring and the sharpening sociospatial inequality and violence in the country. item.title: Vibe Coding: Make Your Own Interactive Story with AI — Wed Nov 25, 6:00 PM — North York Central Library
item.description: What if you could write a story where the reader chooses what happens, like a branching adventure, a mystery, or a game, and have AI build it with you? In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence, Ryan Kelln , you'll learn "vibe-coding": using an AI coding assistant to build your own interactive story or simple game. You'll design the branches, describe the rules in plain language, test for the tricky edge cases (what if the player picks the weird option?), and end up with a single file you can share with anyone. Just a story you want to tell. This is the playful sibling of the practical vibe-coding workshop. Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. item.title: Moonlight Hike - Greenwood North — Wed Nov 25, 7:00 PM
item.description:
GTA Hiking & Stuff Join us for our third moonlight hike of the season. We are posting hikes throughout the year during the nights around the full moon. These hikes are all about the energy of the moon. We can share interesting facts about that months full moon. We will hike at a easy pace doing 5 - 6 km in 2 hrs or less. Please bring a headlamp or a flashlight.
This month we will hike the paths in the Greenwood North Conservation. We will watch the moon rise over the open fields in the park. The moon looks bigger when it rises because of a trick of perception known as the Moon illusion. We can put this illusion to the test if we catch it rising. We are qiut the distance from sity lights at Greenwood North so we can experience a bright moon. The moon can get bright enough to turn off our headlamps while we hike so, let's hope it will be clear night so we can see the sun at night. If you haven't experienced a night hike, come out and enjoy the adventure. Just don't be the last in line.😬

item.title: Total Assault on Culture! FUGS FILM + NOVA '78: DOUBLE FEATURE — Sat Nov 28, 12:30 PM — Paradise Theatre
item.description:
Two films, one afternoon of radical music, art and New York counterculture.
Films We Like presents a special double feature of FUGS FILM and NOVA '78 at Paradise Theatre on November 28, featuring two Q&As with film critic Jason Gorber.
FUGS FILM, directed by Chuck Smith, chronicles The Fugs, the legendary 1960s underground rock band whose provocative music fused poetry, politics and anti-establishment rebellion.
NOVA '78, directed by Aaron Brookner and Rodrigo Areias, transports audiences to the legendary 1978 Nova Convention in New York City. Built from rediscovered archival footage, the film captures a remarkable gathering of countercultural icons including William S. Burroughs, Patti Smith, Frank Zappa, Allen Ginsberg and Laurie Anderson.
Join us for an afternoon celebrating the artists, musicians and troublemakers who helped reshape American culture.

item.title: Understanding Taxes and Benefits — Mon Nov 30, 2:00 PM
item.description:
November is Financial Literacy Month. Presented by West Neighbourhood House , this session will introduce the basics of Canadian personal income tax and discuss the importance of annual tax filing. Participants will also learn about the various benefits for which they may be eligible. Registration: This virtual Zoom event is free to attend. After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing the Zoom link. Need help with Zoom? - Joining and participating in a Zoom webinar - Zoom Privacy Statement Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). The information will only be used for event and program registration, delivery and evaluation. Questions about how the library handles your information can be directed to Answerline staff at answerline@tpl.ca , 416-397-5981, 789 Yonge Street, Toronto ON M4W 2G8.
